title: Regularity and codimension of face strata in complete toric models
statement:
Let $P$ be a sharp fine saturated additive commutative monoid [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], and let $n\ge0$. For a nonzero local ring $L$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_L$ put
$$B_L(P,n)=\varprojlim_N L[P][t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(\mathfrak m_L,z^q\ (q\ne0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)^N,$$
using adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]; $L[P]$ is free over $L$ on $z^q$, with $z^qz^{q'}=z^{q+q'}$. Let $R$ be either $B_k(P,n)$ for a field $k$, or $B_C(P,n)/(\theta)$ for a Cohen ring $C$ of residue characteristic a prime $p$, with uniformizer $p$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring], where
$$\theta-p\in(z^q\ (q\ne0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)B_C(P,n).$$
Write $z^q$ also for the images in $R$. Let $\mathfrak Q$ be any prime ideal of $R$, set $E=R_{\mathfrak Q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and put
$$F=\{q\in P:z^q\notin\mathfrak Q\},\qquad
P_F=\{q-f:q\in P,\ f\in F\}\subseteq P^{\rm gp},\qquad T=P_F/F^{\rm gp}.$$
The set $F$ is a face (a submonoid such that $a+b\in F$ implies $a,b\in F$), and $T$ is sharp fs. Put $J=(z^q:q\in P\setminus F)E$. Then $R$ and $E$ are nonzero Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $E/J$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], and
$$\dim E=\dim(E/J)+\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbf Z}T^{\rm gp}.$$
Dimension and rank have the meanings of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. The assertions include $P=0$, $n=0$, $F=0$, $F=P$ and the zero prime $\mathfrak Q$.

source.place: Agent-formulated local algebra interface for the completed models of Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p.70, in the generization argument of VI 1.3, printed p.69. The localization input referred to there is Kato 1994, 7.1 (WANTED, not read locally); VI does not provide its proof. The node is an unsplit algebraic statement, not a claim that a proof was read.

proof.text:
First treat any sharp fs monoid $H$ and either allowed complete model $A$ of $(H,n)$; we will apply this construction to $H=P$ and to its face $F$. The zero-variable case of [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete] says that the coefficient field or Cohen ring $L$ is nonzero complete regular local, of dimension $0$ or $1$. The monoid $H\oplus\mathbf N^n$ is sharp fs, directly from the componentwise definitions, and its rank is $\operatorname{rank}H^{\rm gp}+n$. Its finite-sum ring is exactly $L[H][t]$, with exactly the completion ideal in this item. Apply [lem-trf-formal-monoid-ring-dimension] to this monoid and $D=L$. In the Cohen case the augmentation of $\theta$ is $p\in pL\setminus p^2L$. Thus the completed ring before the hypersurface is Noetherian local, and
$$\dim A=\operatorname{rank}H^{\rm gp}+n.$$
The hypersurface quotient is nonzero local by [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-local-structure], and Noetherian because every ideal lifts to a finitely generated ideal upstairs. Its normal-domain property is [lem-trf-log-regular-saturation-normality].

source.place: VI 1.6, p.70: completed models; agent algebra using the cited formal-dimension theorem.

proof.text: The completion ideal before the hypersurface is finitely generated: use finite monoid generators, the variables and, over a Cohen ring, $p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] its completion is complete for this extended ideal. By part (2) of the same lemma, the quotient by this extended ideal is $L[H][t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(\mathfrak m_L,z^h\ (h\ne0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)=L/\mathfrak m_L$, a field; so the extended ideal is maximal, and since the ring is local by Step 1 it is the maximal ideal, with residue field $L/\mathfrak m_L$. For the hypersurface, [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-quotient] identifies its completion with the same hypersurface of the completed ring, hence with $A$ itself. The residue of every $z^h$, $h\ne0$, is zero. Consequently the chart $H\to A$ has inverse image of the units equal to $\{0\}$. By [lem-per-complete-local-excellence], $A$ is excellent. Its universal catenarity and the openness of regularity for finite type $A$-algebras are precisely clauses of [def-exc-excellent-ring].

source.place: VI 1.6, p.70; completion inputs: algebra.tex 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated) and completion exactness; excellence is a separately cited theorem.

proof.text: The group $H^{\rm gp}$ is torsion free: if $mg=0$ with $m>0$ and $g=h-h'$, then $mg=0\in H$, so $g\in H$ by saturation, likewise $-g\in H$, and sharpness gives $g=0$. Hence $M_0=\operatorname{Spec}_{\rm mon}H$ is a fine torsion-free monoscheme with a finite affine cover. Apply [lem-trf-toric-normalized-desingularization] to the finite affine monoscheme $M_0=\operatorname{Spec}_{\rm mon}H$ over $\mathbf Q$. Its specified tower has coherent torus-invariant centers and regular last realization. By [lem-trf-monoscheme-toric-tower-descent], this gives a finite saturated monoscheme blowup tower $M_\bullet$ with smooth last monoscheme; this use of a rational realization is solely to obtain the combinatorial tower. Now realize THAT monoid tower over $\mathbf Z$ and base change it to $A$, using [lem-per-integral-toric-tower-proper]. We obtain a proper finite type map $\pi:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ which is an isomorphism on the open $U$ where all chart monomials are invertible. This open is a principal open: invert the product of any finite set of monoid generators. The product is nonzero since $A$ is a domain. Every final affine chart has ring $A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[H]}\mathbf Z[Q]$, with $H\subseteq Q\subseteq H^{\rm gp}$ and $Q^{\rm gp}=H^{\rm gp}$.

source.place: VIII 3.2.19--3.2.20, p.106; integer realization uses VIII 3.2.17--3.2.18, p.105. Agent application to the formal model.

proof.text:
By [lem-trf-monoscheme-smooth-local-charts], refine the final monoid charts to their smallest point neighborhoods. Since $M_r$ is smooth, these section monoids have the form $Q\cong\mathbf N^a\oplus\mathbf Z^b$ by the smoothness definition [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization]. The refinement retains $Q\subset H^{\rm gp}$ and the group-completion isomorphism. Fix a point $y$ of $Y$ above the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$, choose such a chart, and write
$$B=(A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[H]}\mathbf Z[Q])_{\mathfrak q},\qquad V=\{q:z^q\in B^\times\},\qquad T'=Q_V/V^{\rm gp}.$$
The prime $\mathfrak q$ contracts to the maximal ideal of $A$. For [lem-trf-formal-monoid-extension-model], take its base monoid $R=H$, its ring $A$ as here, $G=0$, $S=H$, its sharp chart the given chart, and its unit character identically $1$. Steps 1--2 verify every ring and completion hypothesis; no global log regularity is assumed by that lemma. It identifies $\widehat B$ with $D[[T']]$ or $D[[T']]/(\eta)$ for a nonzero complete regular local $D$, with $\bar\eta\in\mathfrak m_D\setminus\mathfrak m_D^2$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.15--3.1.16, pp.99--100; VI 1.6, p.70, through the independent formal monoid extension theorem.

proof.text: In $Q=\mathbf N^a\oplus\mathbf Z^b$, $V$ contains the group factor. It contains exactly the sums supported on those basis vectors $e_i$ it contains: if such a sum is a unit in a local ring, every factor is a unit, and the converse holds. Thus $T'\cong\mathbf N^s$ for the complementary coordinates. Put $K=D[[T']]$. By [lem-trf-formal-monoid-residue-domain] its maximal ideal is generated by $\mathfrak m_D$ and the $s$ coordinate monomials; its hypotheses hold with the standard embedding $\mathbf N^s\subset\mathbf Z^s$ and the sum-of-coordinates grading. As $D$ is regular, there are $d=\dim D$ generators of $\mathfrak m_D$. By [lem-trf-formal-monoid-ring-dimension], $\dim K=d+s$, so these $d+s$ generators make $K$ regular by [def-weil-regular-scheme]. In the hypersurface case, the augmentation $K\to D$ carries $\mathfrak m_K^2$ into $\mathfrak m_D^2$. Therefore $\eta\notin\mathfrak m_K^2$, and [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-hypersurface-criterion] makes $K/(\eta)$ regular as well. Hence $\widehat B$ is regular. The local ring $B$ is Noetherian (each tensor chart is generated over $A$ by a finite generating tuple of $Q$, so is finite type and Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], and $B$ is its localization at a prime, Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]), so [lem-weil-pbc-completion-regular-local] makes $B$ regular. This proves regularity at every point above the closed base point.

source.place: VI 1.6--1.7, p.70; elementary free-chart cotangent argument from the cited formal-ring theorems.

proof.text: The regular locus of $Y$ is open: each of its finite type affine charts over excellent $A$ has open regular locus by [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Their descriptions agree on overlaps because further prime localizations of a regular local ring are regular, by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization]. Let $Z$ be its closed complement. Since $\pi$ is proper, $\pi(Z)$ is closed by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Step 5 says it omits the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$. A nonempty closed subset of a local spectrum contains its closed point (a proper ideal lies in the maximal ideal). Thus $\pi(Z)$ is empty and $Y$ is regular. Its open $\pi^{-1}U\cong U$ is regular as well, since the local rings of an open subscheme are the same. We have therefore proved, for each of the two models and every sharp fs $H$, regularity of the open obtained by inverting all its chart monomials. This argument has used only the completed chart at the closed base point, not the generization assertion that the present item is meant to prove.

source.place: Agent properness argument using VIII 3.2.17--3.2.20, pp.105--106 and VI 1.6, p.70; it replaces no unit-level route.

proof.text:
Return to the given $R,\mathfrak Q$. The identity $z^{u+v}=z^uz^v$ and primality show that $F$ is a submonoid and that $u+v\in F$ implies $u,v\in F$. By [lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening], $T=P_F/F^{\rm gp}$ is sharp fs and
$$T^{\rm gp}\cong P^{\rm gp}/F^{\rm gp}.$$
This quotient is finite free, so
$$\operatorname{rank}T^{\rm gp}=\operatorname{rank}P^{\rm gp}-\operatorname{rank}F^{\rm gp}.$$
By [lem-trf-complete-model-face-quotients], $\mathfrak p_F=(z^q:q\notin F)R$ is prime and $R/\mathfrak p_F$ is the complete model of $(F,n)$ of the same type (in the Cohen case with the projected $\theta_F$ satisfying the required congruence). Clearly $\mathfrak p_F\subseteq\mathfrak Q$. The fraction map identifies
$$E/J\cong(R/\mathfrak p_F)_{\mathfrak Q/\mathfrak p_F}.$$
Indeed it sends $(r/s)\bmod J$ to $\bar r/\bar s$; denominators are exactly the classes of elements outside $\mathfrak Q$, and its kernel consists of fractions with numerator in $\mathfrak p_F$.

source.place: VI 1.3 and 1.6, pp.69--70; VIII 3.1.1--3.1.5, pp.98--99, for the face operations.

proof.text: The prime $\mathfrak Q/\mathfrak p_F$ of the face model contains none of its surviving monomials: for $f\in F$, $z^f\notin\mathfrak Q$ by definition. Hence it is a point of the monomial-invertible open of that model. Steps 1--6, applied with $H=F$ and the projected Cohen equation when applicable, prove that this open is regular. Thus $E/J$ is regular local by [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Also $E$ is nonzero and local by its fraction construction at a proper prime: an element $r/s$ is invertible exactly when $r\notin\mathfrak Q$, and $1/1$ cannot be zero since that would put $1$ in $\mathfrak Q$. Its Noetherianity follows from [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. The corresponding properties of $R$ were proved in Step 1.

source.place: VI 1.3--1.6, pp.69--70; agent assembly of the regular monomial open and face quotient.

proof.text:
Finally $R$ is a catenary local domain by Steps 1--2 and [def-exc-excellent-ring]. In such a ring, saturated prime chains concatenate: a chain from $(0)$ to a prime $\mathfrak a$ followed by one from $\mathfrak a$ to the maximal ideal is saturated; catenarity makes its length $\dim R$. Similarly for chains ending at $\mathfrak Q$. Write $h(\mathfrak a)=\dim R_{\mathfrak a}$, the maximum chain length from $(0)$ to $\mathfrak a$. These chains have finite maximal lengths since $R$ is Noetherian local. Applying the concatenation first to $\mathfrak p_F\subset\mathfrak m_R$ and then to $\mathfrak p_F\subset\mathfrak Q$ gives
$$h(\mathfrak p_F)=\dim R-\dim(R/\mathfrak p_F),\qquad
\dim E= h(\mathfrak p_F)+\dim(E/J).$$
Step 1 for $H=P$ and $H=F$ says the first difference is $(\operatorname{rank}P^{\rm gp}+n)-(\operatorname{rank}F^{\rm gp}+n)=\operatorname{rank}T^{\rm gp}$, by Step 7. Substitution proves the required equality. This uses only the definition of catenarity and the prime correspondences for localization and quotient, and treats zero-length chains in exactly the same way.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-O1-dfc7087f8 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full: the item (9 steps, statement unchanged from the base), the new node lem-per-integral-toric-tower-proper, and the statements of all 25 cited nodes. Sources checked: ILO VI 1.2-1.8 (pp.69-70; VI 1.6(i)/(ii) gives exactly the k[[P]][[t]] and C(k)[[P]][[t]]/(f), f≡p models) and VIII 3.2.9 and 3.2.17-3.2.20 (pp.104-106). The proof avoids Kato 7.1 generization. It realizes the monoid desingularization tower over Z and base-changes it to A (new node), proves regularity at points over the closed point via formal-monoid-extension-model (G=0, S=H, ε=1), spreads regularity to the whole monomial open by J-2 openness plus the closed image of a proper map, then concludes with face quotients and a catenary chain count. I checked the steps and small cases (k[[x]], C[[x]]/(p-x), the A1 cone, F=0, F=P, P=0, n=0); the dimension and regularity claims hold.
